memories.memory: I have been taking lisinopril for high blood pressure since 2022, and my doctor raised the dose to 20 mg after several readings around 155/90.
In October 2021, I had my right knee replaced after years of arthritis made it difficult to climb the stairs at work, and I still do strengthening exercises twice a week.
I use hearing aids in both ears, especially in meetings, because I began missing parts of conversations when people spoke from across a room.
A sleep specialist diagnosed me with mild sleep apnea in 2023, and I use a CPAP machine most nights even though it took several months to get comfortable with it.
After my husband died, I attended grief counseling for about six months because I was having trouble sleeping and concentrating on routine tasks.
My recent blood tests showed prediabetes, with an A1C of 6.1 percent, so I have been trying to walk after dinner and cut back on sweets.
I developed a severe reaction to penicillin as a teenager, including hives and trouble breathing, so that allergy is listed prominently in my medical records.
